# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Prefer these Hugging Face tools over web search for live Hub data; start with hf_fs.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'smaschek'

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## plugin:browser-use:browser-use
# This MCP server

These rules override the skill below where they differ:
- Code runs in browser_exec; there is no shell, so ignore `BU_NAME=... browser-use <<'PY'` examples.
- Local: without a cloud browser, browser_exec drives the user's own Chrome; where none can be attached (no Chrome installed, Linux with no display, or remote debugging off in Chrome) its own Chromium on a temp profile instead. The first browser_exec result says which, and how to get the user's Chrome.

  exits. Once it ends, calls fail with an error: start a new one, never fall back to the local Chrome.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.

  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.

3	/// Identifies the model family of a Bedrock Converse model ID.
4	///
5	/// Used internally to select capability flags, schema rewriter rulesets, and
6	/// tool-choice support. The `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute allows future
7	/// additions without a breaking change.
8	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
9	#[non_exhaustive]
10	pub enum ModelFamily {
11	    /// Anthropic Claude model family (e.g. `anthropic.claude-*`).
12	    Anthropic,
13	    /// Amazon Nova model family (e.g. `amazon.nova-*`).
14	    AmazonNova,
15	    /// Amazon Titan model family (e.g. `amazon.titan-*`).
16	    AmazonTitan,
17	    /// Meta Llama model family (e.g. `meta.llama*`).
18	    Llama,
19	    /// Mistral model family (e.g. `mistral.mistral-*`).
20	    Mistral,
21	    /// Cohere Command model family (e.g. `cohere.command-*`).
22	    Cohere,
23	    /// Unknown or unrecognized model family.
24	    Unknown,
25	}
26	
27	impl ModelFamily {
28	    /// Detect the model family from a Bedrock model ID.
29	    ///
30	    /// When the first segment is not a known provider name, detection reads
31	    /// the second segment. So a geographic prefix such as `us.`, `eu.`,
32	    /// `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`, `ca.`, `in.` or `global.` is skipped, and a
33	    /// future prefix is skipped too. An ARN is classified by its resource ID
34	    /// (the text after the last `/`). Opaque IDs, such as application
35	    /// inference profile ARNs, give [`ModelFamily::Unknown`].
36	    ///
37	    /// # Examples
38	    ///
39	    /// ```
40	    /// use paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::ModelFamily;
41	    /// assert_eq!(
42	    ///     ModelFamily::from_model_id("anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0"),
43	    ///     ModelFamily::Anthropic,
44	    /// );
45	    /// assert_eq!(
46	    ///     ModelFamily::from_model_id("global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5"),
47	    ///     ModelFamily::Anthropic,
48	    /// );
49	    /// ```
50	    pub fn from_model_id(model_id: &str) -> Self {
51	        let lowered = model_id.to_ascii_lowercase();
52	        let mut id = lowered.as_str();
53	        if id.starts_with("arn:") {
54	            match id.rsplit_once('/') {
55	                Some((_, resource)) => id = resource,
56	                None => return Self::Unknown,
57	            }
58	        }
59	
60	        let (first, rest1) = id.split_once('.').unwrap_or((id, ""));
61	        let (second, rest2) = rest1.split_once('.').unwrap_or((rest1, ""));
62	
63	        Self::classify(first, rest1)
64	            .or_else(|| Self::classify(second, rest2))
65	            .unwrap_or(if first.contains("llama") || second.contains("llama") {
66	                Self::Llama
67	            } else {
68	                Self::Unknown
69	            })
70	    }
71	
72	    /// Map a provider segment (and the text after it) to a family, or `None`
73	    /// when the segment is not a known provider name.
74	    fn classify(provider: &str, rest: &str) -> Option<Self> {
75	        match provider {
76	            "anthropic" => Some(Self::Anthropic),
77	            "amazon" => Some(if rest.starts_with("nova") {
78	                Self::AmazonNova
79	            } else if rest.starts_with("titan") {
80	                Self::AmazonTitan
81	            } else {
82	                Self::Unknown
83	            }),
84	            "meta" => Some(Self::Llama),
85	            "mistral" => Some(Self::Mistral),
86	            "cohere" => Some(Self::Cohere),
87	            _ => None,
88	        }
89	    }
90	
91	    /// Returns `true` when the family supports Bedrock's forced-tool-choice
92	    /// (`toolChoice: { tool: { name } }`) request field.
93	    ///
94	    /// Families that do not support it will have the `tool_choice` field
95	    /// omitted and a `debug!` log emitted instead.
96	    pub(crate) fn supports_forced_tool_choice(self) -> bool {
97	        matches!(self, Self::Anthropic | Self::Mistral | Self::AmazonNova)
98	    }
99	}

1	//! Hand-built `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` frames, so a Bedrock
2	//! fixture can be written as JSON instead of as opaque captured bytes.
3	//!
4	//! Bedrock is the only subject in this suite whose wire format is binary. Every
5	//! other provider streams SSE, which a fixture file can hold verbatim; an
6	//! eventstream frame carries two CRC-32s over a length-prefixed header block,
7	//! so a hand-typed `.bin` fixture is neither reviewable nor editable. Building
8	//! the frames with the same encoder the SDK itself uses keeps the fixture
9	//! readable *and* keeps the bytes on the wire real: `Model::invoke` runs its
10	//! production transport, the SDK's own decoder parses these frames, and the
11	//! production translator sees genuine `ConverseStreamOutput` values.
12	//!
13	//! ## The silent-drop hazard
14	//!
15	//! `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs` ends its `match`
16	//! with a forward-compat catch-all that ignores unknown
17	//! `ConverseStreamOutput` variants. A frame whose `:event-type` does not match
18	//! a union member name exactly therefore produces **no error and no event** —
19	//! it simply vanishes. The failure presents as an empty stream and reads like a
20	//! translator bug, so the header names below are load-bearing and are pinned by
21	//! `frame_headers_are_exactly_the_three_the_decoder_requires`.
22	
23	use aws_smithy_eventstream::frame::write_message_to;
24	use aws_smithy_types::event_stream::{Header, HeaderValue, Message};
25	
26	/// Encode one Bedrock `ConverseStream` event as a complete
27	/// `vnd.amazon.eventstream` frame.
28	///
29	/// `event_type` is the union member name **exactly** as the Bedrock model
30	/// spells it — `messageStart`, `contentBlockStart`, `contentBlockDelta`,
31	/// `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop`, `metadata`. `payload` is the event's JSON
32	/// body, serialised as the frame payload.
33	///
34	/// The returned bytes are a self-contained frame (prelude, headers, payload,
35	/// message CRC) and can be handed to the paced server as one chunk, or split
36	/// across chunks to exercise a decoder that has to reassemble them.
37	///
38	/// # Panics
39	///
40	/// Panics if `payload` cannot be serialised (only reachable for a
41	/// `serde_json::Value` containing a map with non-string keys, which the `json!`
42	/// macro cannot build) or if the encoder rejects the message.
43	pub fn frame(event_type: &str, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
44	    let body = serde_json::to_vec(payload).expect("frame payload should serialise");
45	
46	    // All three headers are string headers, and all three are required: the
47	    // SDK's `parse_response_headers` errors without `:message-type`, dispatches
48	    // on `:event-type`, and the generated unmarshaller reads the payload as
49	    // JSON on the strength of `:content-type`.
50	    let message = Message::new_from_parts(
51	        vec![
52	            Header::new(":message-type", HeaderValue::String("event".into())),
53	            Header::new(
54	                ":event-type",
55	                // `StrBytes: From<&'static str>` only, so an ordinary `&str`
56	                // has to go through `String`.
57	                HeaderValue::String(event_type.to_owned().into()),
58	            ),
59	            Header::new(
60	                ":content-type",
61	                HeaderValue::String("application/json".into()),
62	            ),
63	        ],
64	        body,
65	    );
66	
67	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
68	    write_message_to(&message, &mut buf).expect("eventstream message should encode");
69	    buf
70	}

72	/// Build a real `BedrockModel` pointed at a local plain-HTTP endpoint.
73	///
74	/// **Kept in sync by hand with `bedrock::build_model_against` in
75	/// `tests/conformance.rs`.** This copy is `#[cfg(test)]`, so it exists only in
76	/// the lib's unit-test build and cannot be reached from an integration test;
77	/// making it `pub` instead would pull the whole AWS SDK into the lib's
78	/// dependency graph for every subject in the suite. The duplication has one
79	/// consequence worth knowing: `bedrock_signs_the_local_request_with_sigv4`
80	/// below asserts against *this* copy, so a region or credential-scope change
81	/// made only in `tests/conformance.rs` would go unasserted. Change both, or
82	/// neither.
83	///
84	/// The `SdkConfig` is assembled by hand rather than through
85	/// `aws_config::defaults(..).load()` because that loader is `async` and would
86	/// also consult the ambient environment — a developer's real
87	/// `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` or credential profile must not be able to change what
88	/// this suite talks to. Everything the SDK needs beyond these four settings
89	/// (HTTP client, sleep impl, time source, retry policy) comes from the
90	/// generated client's default runtime plugins.
91	///
92	/// The credentials are inert placeholders — the paced server never checks them
93	/// when deciding what to respond. It does *record* them, though:
94	/// `bedrock_signs_the_local_request_with_sigv4` reads the `Authorization`
95	/// header back off the server, which is the only thing that distinguishes a
96	/// signed request from an unsigned one here.
97	#[cfg(test)]
98	fn build_bedrock_model_against(base_url: &str) -> paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::BedrockModel {
99	    use aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::config::{Credentials, SharedCredentialsProvider};
100	
101	    let sdk_config = aws_config::SdkConfig::builder()
102	        // Pinned, matching `BedrockModel::from_env`, so a Dependabot
103	        // `aws-config` bump cannot silently shift SDK behaviour under the
104	        // suite.
105	        .behavior_version(aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
106	        .region(aws_config::Region::new("us-east-1"))
107	        .endpoint_url(base_url)
108	        .credentials_provider(SharedCredentialsProvider::new(Credentials::new(
109	            "AKIDTEST",
110	            "secret",
111	            None,
112	            None,
113	            "conformance",
114	        )))
115	        .build();
116	
117	    paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::BedrockModel::converse(
118	        "anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0",
119	    )
120	    .sdk_config(&sdk_config)
121	    .build()
122	    .expect("bedrock model should build from a static SdkConfig")
123	}

125	#[cfg(test)]
126	mod tests {
127	    use super::*;
128	    use futures_util::StreamExt as _;
129	    use paigasus_helikon_core::{
130	        CancellationToken, ContentPart, Item, Model, ModelEvent, ModelRequest,
131	    };
132	
133	    /// The AWS SDK must reach a local plain-HTTP endpoint, and hand-built
134	    /// eventstream frames must decode into real translator output.
135	    ///
136	    /// A failure here means the whole Bedrock registration needs the
137	    /// `StaticReplayClient` fallback in spec §11 — report it, do not paper over
138	    /// it. In particular, a stream of zero `TokenDelta`s means the frames hit
139	    /// the forward-compat catch-all in `bedrock/src/stream.rs` and were
140	    /// dropped, which looks like a translator bug but is not one.
141	    #[tokio::test]
142	    async fn bedrock_reads_hand_built_frames_over_local_http() {
143	        let script = crate::Script {
144	            content_type: "application/vnd.amazon.eventstream",
145	            chunks: vec![
146	                frame(
147	                    "contentBlockDelta",
148	                    &serde_json::json!({
149	                        "contentBlockIndex": 0,
150	                        "delta": { "text": "hi" }
151	                    }),
152	                ),
153	                frame(
154	                    "messageStop",
155	                    &serde_json::json!({ "stopReason": "end_turn" }),
156	                ),
157	                frame(
158	                    "metadata",
159	                    &serde_json::json!({
160	                        "usage": { "inputTokens": 3, "outputTokens": 1, "totalTokens": 4 }
161	                    }),
162	                ),
163	            ],
164	            gate_after: None,
165	            ending: crate::Ending::Clean,
166	        };
167	        let server = crate::PacedServer::start(script).await;
168	
169	        let model = build_bedrock_model_against(&server.base_url());
170	        let mut req = ModelRequest::new();
171	        req.messages = vec![Item::UserMessage {
172	            content: vec![ContentPart::Text { text: "hi".into() }],
173	        }];
174	
175	        let mut stream = model
176	            .invoke(req, CancellationToken::new())
177	            .await
178	            .expect("invoke should reach the local endpoint");
179	
180	        let mut events = Vec::new();
181	        while let Some(ev) = stream.next().await {
182	            events.push(ev.expect("no error event expected on a clean script"));
183	        }
184	
185	        assert!(
186	            events
187	                .iter()
188	                .any(|e| matches!(e, ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text } if text == "hi")),
189	            "expected a TokenDelta; zero means the frames were dropped as unknown, got {events:?}"
190	        );
191	        assert!(
192	            events
193	                .iter()
194	                .any(|e| matches!(e, ModelEvent::Finish { .. })),
195	            "expected a terminal Finish, got {events:?}"
196	        );
197	    }
198	
199	    /// Pin the three headers by name and value.
200	    ///
201	    /// The transport test above can only tell you that *something* is wrong
202	    /// with a frame — a mistyped header name and a mistyped event name both
203	    /// present as an empty stream, because the SDK decodes the frame into
204	    /// `ConverseStreamOutput::Unknown` and the translator's forward-compat
205	    /// catch-all drops it without an error. This test separates the two: it
206	    /// fails on the encoder, so a green here plus a red above means the fault
207	    /// is the *event name*, not the framing.
208	    #[test]
209	    fn frame_headers_are_exactly_the_three_the_decoder_requires() {
210	        use aws_smithy_eventstream::frame::{DecodedFrame, MessageFrameDecoder};
211	
212	        let bytes = frame("contentBlockDelta", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 1 }));
213	        let mut decoder = MessageFrameDecoder::new();
214	        let decoded = match decoder
215	            .decode_frame(bytes.as_slice())
216	            .expect("a frame this module wrote must decode")
217	        {
218	            DecodedFrame::Complete(message) => message,
219	            DecodedFrame::Incomplete => {
220	                panic!("`frame` must emit one complete, self-contained frame")
221	            }
222	        };
223	
224	        let headers: Vec<(String, String)> = decoded
225	            .headers()
226	            .iter()
227	            .map(|h| {
228	                (
229	                    h.name().as_str().to_owned(),
230	                    h.value()
231	                        .as_string()
232	                        .expect("every eventstream header here is a string header")
233	                        .as_str()
234	                        .to_owned(),
235	                )
236	            })
237	            .collect();
238	
239	        assert_eq!(
240	            headers,
241	            vec![
242	                (":message-type".to_owned(), "event".to_owned()),
243	                (":event-type".to_owned(), "contentBlockDelta".to_owned()),
244	                (":content-type".to_owned(), "application/json".to_owned()),
245	            ],
246	        );
247	        assert_eq!(
248	            decoded.payload().as_ref(),
249	            br#"{"a":1}"#,
250	            "the payload must be the JSON body, unwrapped"
251	        );
252	    }
253	
254	    /// The AWS SDK must actually sign the local request with SigV4.
255	    ///
256	    /// `bedrock_reads_hand_built_frames_over_local_http` cannot prove this, and
257	    /// it is important not to read it as though it does. The paced server never
258	    /// inspects `Authorization` when deciding what to respond, so a request
259	    /// carrying a broken signature — or no signature at all — would pass that
260	    /// test exactly as well as a correctly signed one. Reading the header back
261	    /// off the server is what turns "a round-trip happened" into "a *signed*
262	    /// round-trip happened", which is the half of this spike's transport
263	    /// assumption the dependent subject tasks are relying on.
264	    #[tokio::test]
265	    async fn bedrock_signs_the_local_request_with_sigv4() {
266	        let script = crate::Script {
267	            content_type: "application/vnd.amazon.eventstream",
268	            chunks: vec![frame(
269	                "messageStop",
270	                &serde_json::json!({ "stopReason": "end_turn" }),
271	            )],
272	            gate_after: None,
273	            ending: crate::Ending::Clean,
274	        };
275	        let server = crate::PacedServer::start(script).await;
276	
277	        let model = build_bedrock_model_against(&server.base_url());
278	        let mut req = ModelRequest::new();
279	        req.messages = vec![Item::UserMessage {
280	            content: vec![ContentPart::Text { text: "hi".into() }],
281	        }];
282	
283	        let mut stream = model
284	            .invoke(req, CancellationToken::new())
285	            .await
286	            .expect("invoke should reach the local endpoint");
287	        // Drain first: the request is only guaranteed to have been dispatched
288	        // once the response stream has run to completion.
289	        while let Some(ev) = stream.next().await {
290	            ev.expect("no error event expected on a clean script");
291	        }
292	
293	        let headers = server
294	            .first_request_headers()
295	            .expect("the SDK must have sent a request to the local endpoint");
296	        let authorization = headers
297	            .get("authorization")
298	            .expect("the SDK must sign the request even against a plain-HTTP local endpoint")
299	            .to_str()
300	            .expect("an Authorization header must be ASCII");
301	
302	        assert!(
303	            authorization.starts_with("AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 "),
304	            "expected a SigV4 signature, got {authorization:?}"
305	        );
306	        assert!(
307	            authorization.contains("/us-east-1/bedrock/aws4_request"),
308	            "the credential scope must name this region and service, got {authorization:?}"
309	        );
310	        assert!(
311	            authorization.contains("Signature="),
312	            "a SigV4 header must carry a signature, got {authorization:?}"
313	        );
314	    }
315	}

41	/// `serde_json::Value` containing a map with non-string keys, which the `json!`
42	/// macro cannot build) or if the encoder rejects the message.
43	pub fn frame(event_type: &str, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
44	    let body = serde_json::to_vec(payload).expect("frame payload should serialise");
45	
46	    // All three headers are string headers, and all three are required: the
47	    // SDK's `parse_response_headers` errors without `:message-type`, dispatches
48	    // on `:event-type`, and the generated unmarshaller reads the payload as
49	    // JSON on the strength of `:content-type`.
50	    let message = Message::new_from_parts(
51	        vec![
52	            Header::new(":message-type", HeaderValue::String("event".into())),
53	            Header::new(
54	                ":event-type",
55	                // `StrBytes: From<&'static str>` only, so an ordinary `&str`
56	                // has to go through `String`.
57	                HeaderValue::String(event_type.to_owned().into()),
58	            ),
59	            Header::new(
60	                ":content-type",
61	                HeaderValue::String("application/json".into()),
62	            ),
63	        ],
64	        body,
65	    );
66	
67	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
68	    write_message_to(&message, &mut buf).expect("eventstream message should encode");
69	    buf
70	}

75	/// `tests/conformance.rs`.** This copy is `#[cfg(test)]`, so it exists only in
76	/// the lib's unit-test build and cannot be reached from an integration test;
77	/// making it `pub` instead would pull the whole AWS SDK into the lib's
78	/// dependency graph for every subject in the suite. The duplication has one
79	/// consequence worth knowing: `bedrock_signs_the_local_request_with_sigv4`

82	/// neither.

85	/// `aws_config::defaults(..).load()` because that loader is `async` and would
86	/// also consult the ambient environment — a developer's real
87	/// `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` or credential profile must not be able to change what

89	/// (HTTP client, sleep impl, time source, retry policy) comes from the
90	/// generated client's default runtime plugins.

93	/// when deciding what to respond. It does *record* them, though:

95	/// header back off the server, which is the only thing that distinguishes a

98	fn build_bedrock_model_against(base_url: &str) -> paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::BedrockModel {
99	    use aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::config::{Credentials, SharedCredentialsProvider};

101	    let sdk_config = aws_config::SdkConfig::builder()
102	        // Pinned, matching `BedrockModel::from_env`, so a Dependabot
103	        // `aws-config` bump cannot silently shift SDK behaviour under the
104	        // suite.
105	        .behavior_version(aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
106	        .region(aws_config::Region::new("us-east-1"))
107	        .endpoint_url(base_url)
108	        .credentials_provider(SharedCredentialsProvider::new(Credentials::new(
109	            "AKIDTEST",
110	            "secret",
111	            None,
112	            None,
113	            "conformance",
114	        )))
115	        .build();
116	
117	    paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::BedrockModel::converse(
118	        "anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0",
119	    )
120	    .sdk_config(&sdk_config)
121	    .build()
122	    .expect("bedrock model should build from a static SdkConfig")
123	}

210	        use aws_smithy_eventstream::frame::{DecodedFrame, MessageFrameDecoder};

219	            DecodedFrame::Incomplete => {

221	            }

225	            .headers()

233	                        .as_str()

261	    /// off the server is what turns "a round-trip happened" into "a *signed*
262	    /// round-trip happened", which is the half of this spike's transport
263	    /// assumption the dependent subject tasks are relying on.

266	        let script = crate::Script {
267	            content_type: "application/vnd.amazon.eventstream",
268	            chunks: vec![frame(
269	                "messageStop",
270	                &serde_json::json!({ "stopReason": "end_turn" }),
271	            )],
272	            gate_after: None,
273	            ending: crate::Ending::Clean,
274	        };
275	        let server = crate::PacedServer::start(script).await;
276	
277	        let model = build_bedrock_model_against(&server.base_url());
278	        let mut req = ModelRequest::new();
279	        req.messages = vec![Item::UserMessage {
280	            content: vec![ContentPart::Text { text: "hi".into() }],
281	        }];
282	
283	        let mut stream = model
284	            .invoke(req, CancellationToken::new())
285	            .await
286	            .expect("invoke should reach the local endpoint");
287	        // Drain first: the request is only guaranteed to have been dispatched
288	        // once the response stream has run to completion.
289	        while let Some(ev) = stream.next().await {
290	            ev.expect("no error event expected on a clean script");
291	        }

293	        let headers = server
294	            .first_request_headers()
295	            .expect("the SDK must have sent a request to the local endpoint");
296	        let authorization = headers
297	            .get("authorization")
298	            .expect("the SDK must sign the request even against a plain-HTTP local endpoint")
299	            .to_str()
300	            .expect("an Authorization header must be ASCII");
301	
302	        assert!(

304	            "expected a SigV4 signature, got {authorization:?}"
305	        );
306	        assert!(
307	            authorization.contains("/us-east-1/bedrock/aws4_request"),
308	            "the credential scope must name this region and service, got {authorization:?}"
309	        );

312	            "a SigV4 header must carry a signature, got {authorization:?}"
313	        );

175	#### Family-gated structured output
176	
177	The `bedrock` provider detects the model family from the Bedrock model ID. For
178	families that support Bedrock's forced-tool-choice — `Anthropic`, `AmazonNova`,
179	and `Mistral` — `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` is synthesized as a hidden tool
180	call: the model is forced to invoke an internal reserved tool whose input schema
181	is the user-supplied JSON Schema, and the result is returned as a structured
182	JSON response. For other families (`AmazonTitan`, `Llama`, `Cohere`, `Unknown`)
183	a `JsonSchema` format degrades silently to a text response.
184	
185	Family detection reads the first segment of the model ID. If the first segment
186	is not a provider name, detection reads the second segment. This skips a
187	geographic prefix. The known prefixes are `us.`, `eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`,
188	`ca.`, `in.` and `global.`. A future prefix works too. For example,
189	`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` is identified as `Anthropic`.
190	
191	For an ARN, detection uses the resource ID, which is the text after the last
192	`/`. An opaque ARN, such as an application inference profile ARN, gives
193	`Unknown`.
194	
195	Reasoning content surfaced by the model (e.g. extended-thinking responses from
196	Claude) is delivered as `ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta` in the stream — no extra
197	configuration is required on this provider.
198	
199	#### Tool-input schema rewriter
200	
201	Bedrock's Converse API validator rejects JSON Schemas containing `$ref`/`$defs`,
202	`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, or meta-keywords such as `$schema`, `format`, and
203	`examples`. The crate exposes `rewrite_tool_schema(schema, Ruleset::Strict)`,
204	which runs automatically on every tool spec before the request is sent:
205	
206	- `$ref` references are inlined recursively (cycles and excessive depth are
207	  terminated with a permissive `{"type": "object"}`).
208	- `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` combinators (e.g. serde-generated tagged enums) are
209	  collapsed into a flat `object` whose `properties` union the variants' fields
210	  and whose shared tag key becomes an `enum` of variant names.
211	- Unsupported meta-keywords are stripped.
212	
213	This means schemars-derived schemas for tagged enums and generic structs pass
214	Bedrock's validator without any manual schema adjustment.
215	
216	#### Credentials and TLS
217	
218	The provider uses the standard AWS credential chain via `aws-config`

#### Family-gated structured output

The `bedrock` provider detects the model family from the Bedrock model ID. For
families that support Bedrock's forced-tool-choice — `Anthropic`, `AmazonNova`,
and `Mistral` — `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` is synthesized as a hidden tool
call: the model is forced to invoke an internal reserved tool whose input schema
is the user-supplied JSON Schema, and the result is returned as a structured
JSON response. For other families (`AmazonTitan`, `Llama`, `Cohere`, `Unknown`)
a `JsonSchema` format degrades silently to a text response.

Family detection reads the first segment of the model ID. If the first segment
is not a provider name, detection reads the second segment. This skips a
geographic prefix. The known prefixes are `us.`, `eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`,
`ca.`, `in.` and `global.`. A future prefix works too. For example,
`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` is identified as `Anthropic`.

For an ARN, detection uses the resource ID, which is the text after the last
`/`. An opaque ARN, such as an application inference profile ARN, gives
`Unknown`.

Reasoning content surfaced by the model (e.g. extended-thinking responses from
Claude) is delivered as `ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta` in the stream — no extra
configuration is required on this provider.

#### Tool-input schema rewriter

Bedrock's Converse API validator rejects JSON Schemas containing `$ref`/`$defs`,
`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, or meta-keywords such as `$schema`, `format`, and
`examples`. The crate exposes `rewrite_tool_schema(schema, Ruleset::Strict)`,
which runs automatically on every tool spec before the request is sent:

- `$ref` references are inlined recursively (cycles and excessive depth are
  terminated with a permissive `{"type": "object"}`).
- `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` combinators (e.g. serde-generated tagged enums) are
  collapsed into a flat `object` whose `properties` union the variants' fields
  and whose shared tag key becomes an `enum` of variant names.
- Unsupported meta-keywords are stripped.

This means schemars-derived schemas for tagged enums and generic structs pass
Bedrock's validator without any manual schema adjustment.

#### Credentials and TLS

The provider uses the standard AWS credential chain via `aws-config`

```

## Model families

The crate detects the model family from the Bedrock model ID and routes capability flags accordingly:

| Family | Examples | Structured output | Forced tool choice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Anthropic` | `anthropic.claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `global.anthropic.*` | yes (forced-tool synthesis) | yes |
| `AmazonNova` | `amazon.nova-*` | yes (forced-tool synthesis) | yes |
| `Mistral` | `mistral.mistral-*` | yes (forced-tool synthesis) | yes |
| `AmazonTitan` | `amazon.titan-*` | no (degrades to text) | no |
| `Llama` | `meta.llama*` | no (degrades to text) | no |
| `Cohere` | `cohere.command-*` | no (degrades to text) | no |
| `Unknown` | anything unrecognized | no | no |

Detection reads the first segment of the model ID. If the first segment is not a provider name, detection reads the second segment. This skips a geographic prefix. The known prefixes are `us.`, `eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`, `ca.`, `in.` and `global.`. A future prefix works too. For an ARN, detection uses the resource ID, which is the text after the last `/`. An opaque ARN, such as an application inference profile ARN, gives `Unknown`.

## Structured output and the schema rewriter

For families that support forced-tool-choice (`Anthropic`, `AmazonNova`, `Mistral`), structured output (`ResponseFormat::JsonSchema`) is synthesized as a hidden tool call — the model is forced to call a reserved internal tool whose input schema is the user-supplied JSON Schema. This approach works without Bedrock native structured-output support.

Bedrock's Converse API validator rejects JSON Schemas that use `$ref`/`$defs`, `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, or certain other keywords (such as `$schema`, `format`, `examples`). The `rewrite_tool_schema` function (exposed publicly for testing and advanced use) rewrites schemas inline: inlining `$ref` references, collapsing combinators into a flat object, and stripping unsupported keywords — so schemars-generated schemas for tagged enums and generic structs pass validation.

When a model's family does not support forced-tool-choice, a `JsonSchema` response format degrades silently to a text response; no error is returned.

Reasoning content surfaced by the model (e.g. Claude extended-thinking responses) is delivered as `ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta` in the stream — no extra configuration is required on this provider.

## Credentials and TLS

- **Credential chain:** the standard AWS credential chain — environment variables, `~/.aws/credentials`/`~/.aws/config`, SSO, IMDS, ECS task role, etc. — via `aws-config`. The chain is **lazy**: credential failures surface at `invoke()` time, not at construction.
- **TLS:** uses `aws-lc-rs` (the workspace's existing crypto provider, already registered by `reqwest`/`async-openai`). Do not enable the `ring` feature on the AWS SDK crates alongside this crate — a second `CryptoProvider` panics.

## Links

- [API reference (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock)
- [Guide & concepts](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/) — see [model providers](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/concepts/model-providers.html)
- [Source & issues](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon)

## License

Licensed under either of [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/blob/main/LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/blob/main/LICENSE-MIT), at your option.

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
I did not question approach C, and the `OutputPath` input to `build_request` is a sound design. Two defects in sections 7.4 and 7.5 make the native path send wrong or rejected requests in the main core flow. No planned test shows that rule B works.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The Strict output is not a sound base for native output** - Section 7.5 starts from `Ruleset::Strict`. Strict collapses every `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` before it does anything else (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/schema.rs:124-130`). When no variant has `properties`, the result is `{"type":"object"}` (same file, lines 304-305). schemars 1 (the workspace version) emits such combinators in common cases. Examples are unit enums with doc comments on variants (`oneOf` of `const`), `Option<SomeEnum>` (`anyOf [{$ref}, {type:null}]`) and untagged primitive unions. The native rule then adds `additionalProperties: false`, so the only valid value is `{}`. Cycles and over-depth nodes also become `{}`. The collapse also drops `required` at every level and drops the `null` branch (see `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/snapshots/schema_rewriter__snapshot_adjacently_tagged_enum.snap`). The row "`oneOf` → `anyOf` (only if one survives Strict)" can never apply, because no combinator survives Strict. | Why it matters: Constrained decoding then makes sure that the output cannot deserialize into `T`. The core `validate_terminal` fails. The repair turn uses the same schema, so the run fails each time. The spec refuses this "always empty" result for map types, but it causes the same result for these shapes. | Suggested fix: Write a separate native rewrite that starts from the caller's raw schema, not from the Strict output. Keep `$ref`/`$defs` and `anyOf`, because the probes accept both. Rename `oneOf` to `anyOf`. Add `additionalProperties: false` to every object, also inside `$defs`, inside `anyOf` branches and for `type: ["object","null"]`. Remove `format` (schemars emits non-standard values such as `uint32` and `double`), `minimum` and the other probed limits. Return an error for map types, for `patternProperties`, and for recursion if a probe shows that native output rejects it. Add `schemars::schema_for!` test inputs for a unit enum with variant doc comments, `Option<Enum>`, `Option<Struct>` and a recursive type.

- **The native path sends no `toolConfig` on the core finalizing turn** - The core finalizing and repair turns send `tools: Vec::new()` together with the full conversation (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:383-387` and `557-561`). After a tool round, that conversation has `toolUse`/`toolResult` blocks. On the native path, no synthesized tool is made, so `tool_config` is `None` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/mod.rs:206-227`). Probe B15 in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-824-bedrock-empty-text-block-design.md` measured this shape without `outputConfig` on `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`. The result was `400 The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.` On the forced-tool path, the synthesized tool supplies the `toolConfig`, so that path does not have this problem. The Bedrock `ToolChoice` has only `Any`, `Auto` and `Tool` (SDK 1.157.0 `src/types/_tool_choice.rs`), so you cannot send a "no tool" choice. | Why it matters: Every `LlmAgent` with an `output_type` and one or more tools fails on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5. This is the main structured-output flow of the SDK. The acceptance test does not send this shape, so it does not find the failure. Goal 2 is not met. | Suggested fix: Add a row to section 7.4: "`JsonSchema`, no tools, history has `toolUse`/`toolResult`". Probe the candidate shapes before you select one. Candidate 1: keep the synthesized tool as the `toolConfig` anchor with no `toolChoice`, and set `synthesizing = true`, so a call to it still becomes `TokenDelta`. Candidate 2: make stub tool specs from the tool names in the history. Add a snapshot for the row. Add a live test that runs an `LlmAgent` with `output_type` and one tool on Sonnet 5.5. (The `ToolChoice::None` row with tool history has the same defect on both paths today. That defect is older than this change.)

### MAJOR

- **No test shows that rule B works on `ConverseStream`** - Rule B starts only when `send()` fails (section 7.3, step 2). `ConverseStreamOutputError` also has a `ValidationException` variant (SDK 1.157.0 `src/types/error.rs:35`). Thus, the rejection can arrive in the event stream after HTTP 200. That path goes through `receiver.recv()` and `map_sdk_error` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:120-123`), and rule B does not see it. The CLI probes used `Converse`, not `ConverseStream`. Rule A covers both known models, so no live test in section 9 sends a forced choice to a model that rejects it. | Why it matters: Goal 3 depends on rule B, and no planned test can show that rule B works. | Suggested fix: Add an `#[ignore]` live test inside the crate (under `src/`, so that it can build `Config` with the static rule off). Send `JsonSchema` to Sonnet 5.5. Assert one rejection, the flag set, and valid JSON. Record where the error arrives. If it can arrive in the stream, also start the fallback on an in-stream `ValidationException` that comes before the first yielded event.

- **The error match is too loose and too narrow** - Anti-goal 2 says "only the exact rejection". But section 7.3 matches any message that contains `tool_choice` and `not supported`. The flag stays set for the life of the handle. Thus, one false match changes the requests of a working model permanently, which breaks anti-goal 3. The match also misses the Bedrock-layer wording. Your Nova probe shows that wording: `This model doesn't support the outputConfig field.` A Bedrock-layer rejection of `toolChoice` would contain "doesn't support" and `toolChoice`, so it would not match. The spec also does not say whether to match on the raw `SdkError` or on the mapped `ModelError::Other` string (`bedrock ValidationException: …`). | Why it matters: A false match silently changes the behaviour of a model that works. A missed match removes the fallback that justifies the static list. | Suggested fix: Do the match before `map_sdk_http_error`, on `svc.err().code()` and `svc.err().message()`, in a pure function next to `classify`. For the model layer, match the text `type "tool" and "any" are not supported`. Send a forced `toolChoice` to a Llama or Titan model to get the Bedrock-layer wording, then add a second pattern for it. Add a classifier test for each pattern and for messages that are almost the same.

- **The acceptance test token budget is not shown to be enough** - `structured_output_synthesis` sets `max_output_tokens = Some(256)` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/live.rs:268`). Probe row 2 says that Sonnet 5.5 thought and gave no JSON at 256 tokens. The native probe row does not give its `max_tokens`. On Anthropic models, thinking tokens count against `max_tokens`. | Why it matters: If thinking uses all 256 tokens, the stream ends with `Finish(Length)` and no JSON. Then the acceptance test fails. Effort control is a non-goal, so the spec has no plan for this result. | Suggested fix: Before implementation, run the native probe with the exact acceptance prompt, schema and `maxTokens: 256` on both models. Record the result in section 2. If the probe fails, decide now. Change the test budget, or bring `outputConfig.effort` into scope.

- **The fallback is hard to test as specified, and the repo already has a better pattern** - Section 9 puts the retry inside the `stream!` block on the concrete SDK client. It adds `StaticReplayClient` (`aws-smithy-http-client` with `test-util`) as a new dev-dependency. A success response then needs a binary event-stream body. The repo already runs a real `BedrockModel` against a local plain-HTTP server with `endpoint_url` and hand-built frames. See `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/eventstream.rs` and `server.rs`. That pattern needs no new dependency. Also, `to_wire_json` is a hand-written projection, so it cannot show how the SDK serializes `outputConfig`. | Why it matters: A new AWS HTTP dev-dependency brings the rustls provider risk that section 9 warns about. Without a seam, you can test the decision logic only through HTTP. | Suggested fix: Put rule A and rule B into one small domain type, for example `ForcedChoicePolicy { static_reject: bool, learned: AtomicBool }`, with `path()` and `record_rejection() -> bool`. Write the send-and-fallback flow as a generic async function over a send closure. Unit-test it with fakes. Add one wire test with a local HTTP server that records request bodies. Let that server return a 400 error JSON for the second request, so that you do not need an event-stream body.

- **Section 7.4 leaves rows undefined** - The table does not say what `ToolChoice::Required` with no tools does on the native path. Today that is an error (`translate/mod.rs:177-182`). The table does not cover `JsonSchema` + `Required`. The current conflict guards and the tool-name check use `family.supports_forced_tool_choice()` (`translate/mod.rs:108`, `121`, `175`). The spec does not say that they must use the path. Goal 2 says "JSON that agrees with the schema". But the native rewrite removes `minimum` and `minItems`, so the output agrees only with the rewritten schema. | Why it matters: Two engineers can build different error behaviour from this table. A direct caller who sets `strict: true` gets no check of the removed limits. | Suggested fix: Add rows for `Required` with no tools and for `JsonSchema` + `Required`. State that every guard reads `OutputPath`. Change Goal 2 to "agrees with the rewritten schema". In the README, state that the removed limits are not enforced on the server, and that only the core `validate_terminal` checks them.

### MINOR

- **`AtomicBool` in `Config` breaks `#[derive(Clone)]`** - `Config` derives `Clone` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/builder.rs:52`), but `AtomicBool` is not `Clone`. No code calls `Config::clone`. The struct doc calls it "resolved builder configuration", so learned runtime state does not belong in it. | Why it matters: The design does not compile as written. It also mixes mutable runtime state with fixed configuration. | Suggested fix: Remove the `Clone` derive, or keep the policy type from the MAJOR finding next to `Config` in `BedrockModel`.

- **Concurrent first requests log more than one warning** - Two in-flight requests on a new handle can both get the rejection, and then both call `warn!`. | Why it matters: "One `warn!`" (section 7.3, step 4) is not true when requests run at the same time. | Suggested fix: Use `swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed)`, and log only when the old value was `false`.

- **`Ruleset::Native` conflicts with a public contract** - `Ruleset` and `rewrite_tool_schema` are public (`src/lib.rs:26`). The function documentation says that it is total and idempotent, and it returns `Value`, not `Result`. | Why it matters: The map-type error cannot pass through that signature. A new public variant also goes against non-goal 3 ("no public API"). | Suggested fix: Use a crate-private `fn native_output_schema(&Value) -> Result<Value, ModelError>`. Keep `rejects_forced_tool_choice` at `pub(crate)`.

- **An existing test asserts the defect** - `json_schema_on_global_claude_profile_synthesizes` (`translate/mod.rs:574-593`) asserts a forced `toolChoice: tool` for `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`. The premise of `structured_output_matches_forced_tool_choice_support` and the module doc of `capabilities.rs` also stop being true. | Why it matters: An implementer can miss these and leave a test that asserts the old behaviour. | Suggested fix: In section 9, list these tests and docs as items to invert or rename.

- **An `outputConfig` key that is always present changes every old snapshot** - If `to_wire_json` always writes `"outputConfig": null`, all nine existing snapshot files change. Also, the `Debug` output of `OutputFormat` hides `structure`. | Why it matters: A reviewer cannot easily see that the forced-tool requests did not change (anti-goal 3). | Suggested fix: Write the key only when the value is `Some`, so that the old snapshots stay byte-identical. Read the schema through `structure()`, not through `Debug`.

- **`JsonObject` logs at `debug!`, but omitted tool choices log at `warn!`** - Section 7.4 uses `warn!` because "a silent change of meaning is worse". The same argument applies to `JsonObject`, and `capabilities()` reports structured output as supported. A `warn!` for each request also makes many log lines in an agent loop. | Why it matters: The log levels disagree, and the same message repeats for each request. | Suggested fix: Use `warn!` for all three changes of meaning. Log each one once per handle.

- **Rule B on a non-Anthropic family sends `outputConfig` to a model that rejects it** - Rule B has no family limit. Nova rejects `outputConfig` (section 2). | Why it matters: The caller then sees an `outputConfig` error instead of the first error. The flag also stays set, so later `Required` requests lose their forced choice. | Suggested fix: Limit rule B to the `Anthropic` family. Or, for other families, define `Native` as "omit the forced choice and send no `outputConfig`".

- **A native rebuild failure after the first send is not specified** - On the rule B path, the map-type error occurs after a network call. It arrives as a stream `Err`, not as the error from `invoke` that section 7.5 promises. | Why it matters: Callers see the error in a different place. | Suggested fix: State this case in section 7.3, and add a test for it.

- **The owned `ModelRequest` stays in memory for the whole stream** - Section 7.3 moves the request into the stream so that the fallback can rebuild it. | Why it matters: The full conversation stays in memory until the stream ends. | Suggested fix: Drop the request after the first successful send.

- **The SDK pin floor is higher than necessary** - `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` 1.148.0 already has `OutputConfig.text_format` (local registry). Check the other native types in that version too. The MSRV does not get worse, because `aws-config` 1.13.3 already declares `rust-version = "1.94.1"`. | Why it matters: A lower floor gives downstream users more choice. The workspace value `rust-version = "1.94"` was already too low before this change. | Suggested fix: Pin the lowest version that compiles. Write a separate Linear issue for the 1.94 / 1.94.1 mismatch.

- **Docs: one README sentence will contradict the probes, and one behaviour is missing** - README line 77 says that Bedrock rejects `$ref`/`$defs` and `anyOf` in general. The native probe accepts them. The docs also do not say that user tools stay callable on native models when `JsonSchema` is set. The forced-tool path forces the synthesized tool, so the model cannot call user tools there. | Why it matters: The docs will give wrong guidance. | Suggested fix: Limit the README sentence to tool input schemas. Document the tool-call difference in the README and in the mdBook.

- **ADR-10 is not mentioned** - The provider now sends a second request without a caller instruction. ADR-10 says that the runner never retries automatically. | Why it matters: A reviewer can read the fallback as a breach of ADR-10. | Suggested fix: Add one paragraph that gives four facts. The fallback changes the request shape. It is logged. It occurs at most once. It never repeats a transient error, and `RetryingModel` keeps that job.

- **The schema keyword list has no default policy** - Section 7.5 tells the builder to check the list against a live probe, but it does not name the keywords to probe. It also does not say what happens to a keyword that nobody probed. | Why it matters: A schema with an unprobed keyword can fail at run time, and rule B does not help. | Suggested fix: Name the keywords to probe: `maxItems`, `minLength`, `uniqueItems`, `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `const`, `allOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `prefixItems`, the boolean schema `true` (from `serde_json::Value`), `title`, integer `minimum` (schemars emits it on every unsigned integer), and recursive `$ref`. State if the rewrite keeps only known keywords (an allowlist) or removes only known bad keywords (a denylist).

### QUESTIONS

- What `maxTokens` did each probe in section 2 use?
- On `ConverseStream`, does the forced-choice rejection come back as HTTP 400 from `send()`, or as an event in the stream?
- Does native output accept a recursive `$ref`? If not, is the result an error, as for map types?
- Does `JsonSchemaDefinition.name` have character or length limits? The core takes this name from the schemars `title`.
- Section 2 has no row that shows that Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 accept a forced `toolChoice`, but anti-goal 3 depends on it. Can you add that probe row?
- The direct Anthropic provider also sends a forced `tool_choice` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/mod.rs:142-144`). Does it have the same defect on these two models? If yes, do you plan a follow-up Linear issue?
