## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
I did not question approach C, and the `OutputPath` input to `build_request` is a sound design. Two defects in sections 7.4 and 7.5 make the native path send wrong or rejected requests in the main core flow. No planned test shows that rule B works.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The Strict output is not a sound base for native output** - Section 7.5 starts from `Ruleset::Strict`. Strict collapses every `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` before it does anything else (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/schema.rs:124-130`). When no variant has `properties`, the result is `{"type":"object"}` (same file, lines 304-305). schemars 1 (the workspace version) emits such combinators in common cases. Examples are unit enums with doc comments on variants (`oneOf` of `const`), `Option<SomeEnum>` (`anyOf [{$ref}, {type:null}]`) and untagged primitive unions. The native rule then adds `additionalProperties: false`, so the only valid value is `{}`. Cycles and over-depth nodes also become `{}`. The collapse also drops `required` at every level and drops the `null` branch (see `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/snapshots/schema_rewriter__snapshot_adjacently_tagged_enum.snap`). The row "`oneOf` → `anyOf` (only if one survives Strict)" can never apply, because no combinator survives Strict. | Why it matters: Constrained decoding then makes sure that the output cannot deserialize into `T`. The core `validate_terminal` fails. The repair turn uses the same schema, so the run fails each time. The spec refuses this "always empty" result for map types, but it causes the same result for these shapes. | Suggested fix: Write a separate native rewrite that starts from the caller's raw schema, not from the Strict output. Keep `$ref`/`$defs` and `anyOf`, because the probes accept both. Rename `oneOf` to `anyOf`. Add `additionalProperties: false` to every object, also inside `$defs`, inside `anyOf` branches and for `type: ["object","null"]`. Remove `format` (schemars emits non-standard values such as `uint32` and `double`), `minimum` and the other probed limits. Return an error for map types, for `patternProperties`, and for recursion if a probe shows that native output rejects it. Add `schemars::schema_for!` test inputs for a unit enum with variant doc comments, `Option<Enum>`, `Option<Struct>` and a recursive type.

- **The native path sends no `toolConfig` on the core finalizing turn** - The core finalizing and repair turns send `tools: Vec::new()` together with the full conversation (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:383-387` and `557-561`). After a tool round, that conversation has `toolUse`/`toolResult` blocks. On the native path, no synthesized tool is made, so `tool_config` is `None` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/mod.rs:206-227`). Probe B15 in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-824-bedrock-empty-text-block-design.md` measured this shape without `outputConfig` on `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`. The result was `400 The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks.` On the forced-tool path, the synthesized tool supplies the `toolConfig`, so that path does not have this problem. The Bedrock `ToolChoice` has only `Any`, `Auto` and `Tool` (SDK 1.157.0 `src/types/_tool_choice.rs`), so you cannot send a "no tool" choice. | Why it matters: Every `LlmAgent` with an `output_type` and one or more tools fails on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5. This is the main structured-output flow of the SDK. The acceptance test does not send this shape, so it does not find the failure. Goal 2 is not met. | Suggested fix: Add a row to section 7.4: "`JsonSchema`, no tools, history has `toolUse`/`toolResult`". Probe the candidate shapes before you select one. Candidate 1: keep the synthesized tool as the `toolConfig` anchor with no `toolChoice`, and set `synthesizing = true`, so a call to it still becomes `TokenDelta`. Candidate 2: make stub tool specs from the tool names in the history. Add a snapshot for the row. Add a live test that runs an `LlmAgent` with `output_type` and one tool on Sonnet 5.5. (The `ToolChoice::None` row with tool history has the same defect on both paths today. That defect is older than this change.)

### MAJOR

- **No test shows that rule B works on `ConverseStream`** - Rule B starts only when `send()` fails (section 7.3, step 2). `ConverseStreamOutputError` also has a `ValidationException` variant (SDK 1.157.0 `src/types/error.rs:35`). Thus, the rejection can arrive in the event stream after HTTP 200. That path goes through `receiver.recv()` and `map_sdk_error` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:120-123`), and rule B does not see it. The CLI probes used `Converse`, not `ConverseStream`. Rule A covers both known models, so no live test in section 9 sends a forced choice to a model that rejects it. | Why it matters: Goal 3 depends on rule B, and no planned test can show that rule B works. | Suggested fix: Add an `#[ignore]` live test inside the crate (under `src/`, so that it can build `Config` with the static rule off). Send `JsonSchema` to Sonnet 5.5. Assert one rejection, the flag set, and valid JSON. Record where the error arrives. If it can arrive in the stream, also start the fallback on an in-stream `ValidationException` that comes before the first yielded event.

- **The error match is too loose and too narrow** - Anti-goal 2 says "only the exact rejection". But section 7.3 matches any message that contains `tool_choice` and `not supported`. The flag stays set for the life of the handle. Thus, one false match changes the requests of a working model permanently, which breaks anti-goal 3. The match also misses the Bedrock-layer wording. Your Nova probe shows that wording: `This model doesn't support the outputConfig field.` A Bedrock-layer rejection of `toolChoice` would contain "doesn't support" and `toolChoice`, so it would not match. The spec also does not say whether to match on the raw `SdkError` or on the mapped `ModelError::Other` string (`bedrock ValidationException: …`). | Why it matters: A false match silently changes the behaviour of a model that works. A missed match removes the fallback that justifies the static list. | Suggested fix: Do the match before `map_sdk_http_error`, on `svc.err().code()` and `svc.err().message()`, in a pure function next to `classify`. For the model layer, match the text `type "tool" and "any" are not supported`. Send a forced `toolChoice` to a Llama or Titan model to get the Bedrock-layer wording, then add a second pattern for it. Add a classifier test for each pattern and for messages that are almost the same.

- **The acceptance test token budget is not shown to be enough** - `structured_output_synthesis` sets `max_output_tokens = Some(256)` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/live.rs:268`). Probe row 2 says that Sonnet 5.5 thought and gave no JSON at 256 tokens. The native probe row does not give its `max_tokens`. On Anthropic models, thinking tokens count against `max_tokens`. | Why it matters: If thinking uses all 256 tokens, the stream ends with `Finish(Length)` and no JSON. Then the acceptance test fails. Effort control is a non-goal, so the spec has no plan for this result. | Suggested fix: Before implementation, run the native probe with the exact acceptance prompt, schema and `maxTokens: 256` on both models. Record the result in section 2. If the probe fails, decide now. Change the test budget, or bring `outputConfig.effort` into scope.

- **The fallback is hard to test as specified, and the repo already has a better pattern** - Section 9 puts the retry inside the `stream!` block on the concrete SDK client. It adds `StaticReplayClient` (`aws-smithy-http-client` with `test-util`) as a new dev-dependency. A success response then needs a binary event-stream body. The repo already runs a real `BedrockModel` against a local plain-HTTP server with `endpoint_url` and hand-built frames. See `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/eventstream.rs` and `server.rs`. That pattern needs no new dependency. Also, `to_wire_json` is a hand-written projection, so it cannot show how the SDK serializes `outputConfig`. | Why it matters: A new AWS HTTP dev-dependency brings the rustls provider risk that section 9 warns about. Without a seam, you can test the decision logic only through HTTP. | Suggested fix: Put rule A and rule B into one small domain type, for example `ForcedChoicePolicy { static_reject: bool, learned: AtomicBool }`, with `path()` and `record_rejection() -> bool`. Write the send-and-fallback flow as a generic async function over a send closure. Unit-test it with fakes. Add one wire test with a local HTTP server that records request bodies. Let that server return a 400 error JSON for the second request, so that you do not need an event-stream body.

- **Section 7.4 leaves rows undefined** - The table does not say what `ToolChoice::Required` with no tools does on the native path. Today that is an error (`translate/mod.rs:177-182`). The table does not cover `JsonSchema` + `Required`. The current conflict guards and the tool-name check use `family.supports_forced_tool_choice()` (`translate/mod.rs:108`, `121`, `175`). The spec does not say that they must use the path. Goal 2 says "JSON that agrees with the schema". But the native rewrite removes `minimum` and `minItems`, so the output agrees only with the rewritten schema. | Why it matters: Two engineers can build different error behaviour from this table. A direct caller who sets `strict: true` gets no check of the removed limits. | Suggested fix: Add rows for `Required` with no tools and for `JsonSchema` + `Required`. State that every guard reads `OutputPath`. Change Goal 2 to "agrees with the rewritten schema". In the README, state that the removed limits are not enforced on the server, and that only the core `validate_terminal` checks them.

### MINOR

- **`AtomicBool` in `Config` breaks `#[derive(Clone)]`** - `Config` derives `Clone` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/builder.rs:52`), but `AtomicBool` is not `Clone`. No code calls `Config::clone`. The struct doc calls it "resolved builder configuration", so learned runtime state does not belong in it. | Why it matters: The design does not compile as written. It also mixes mutable runtime state with fixed configuration. | Suggested fix: Remove the `Clone` derive, or keep the policy type from the MAJOR finding next to `Config` in `BedrockModel`.

- **Concurrent first requests log more than one warning** - Two in-flight requests on a new handle can both get the rejection, and then both call `warn!`. | Why it matters: "One `warn!`" (section 7.3, step 4) is not true when requests run at the same time. | Suggested fix: Use `swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed)`, and log only when the old value was `false`.

- **`Ruleset::Native` conflicts with a public contract** - `Ruleset` and `rewrite_tool_schema` are public (`src/lib.rs:26`). The function documentation says that it is total and idempotent, and it returns `Value`, not `Result`. | Why it matters: The map-type error cannot pass through that signature. A new public variant also goes against non-goal 3 ("no public API"). | Suggested fix: Use a crate-private `fn native_output_schema(&Value) -> Result<Value, ModelError>`. Keep `rejects_forced_tool_choice` at `pub(crate)`.

- **An existing test asserts the defect** - `json_schema_on_global_claude_profile_synthesizes` (`translate/mod.rs:574-593`) asserts a forced `toolChoice: tool` for `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`. The premise of `structured_output_matches_forced_tool_choice_support` and the module doc of `capabilities.rs` also stop being true. | Why it matters: An implementer can miss these and leave a test that asserts the old behaviour. | Suggested fix: In section 9, list these tests and docs as items to invert or rename.

- **An `outputConfig` key that is always present changes every old snapshot** - If `to_wire_json` always writes `"outputConfig": null`, all nine existing snapshot files change. Also, the `Debug` output of `OutputFormat` hides `structure`. | Why it matters: A reviewer cannot easily see that the forced-tool requests did not change (anti-goal 3). | Suggested fix: Write the key only when the value is `Some`, so that the old snapshots stay byte-identical. Read the schema through `structure()`, not through `Debug`.

- **`JsonObject` logs at `debug!`, but omitted tool choices log at `warn!`** - Section 7.4 uses `warn!` because "a silent change of meaning is worse". The same argument applies to `JsonObject`, and `capabilities()` reports structured output as supported. A `warn!` for each request also makes many log lines in an agent loop. | Why it matters: The log levels disagree, and the same message repeats for each request. | Suggested fix: Use `warn!` for all three changes of meaning. Log each one once per handle.

- **Rule B on a non-Anthropic family sends `outputConfig` to a model that rejects it** - Rule B has no family limit. Nova rejects `outputConfig` (section 2). | Why it matters: The caller then sees an `outputConfig` error instead of the first error. The flag also stays set, so later `Required` requests lose their forced choice. | Suggested fix: Limit rule B to the `Anthropic` family. Or, for other families, define `Native` as "omit the forced choice and send no `outputConfig`".

- **A native rebuild failure after the first send is not specified** - On the rule B path, the map-type error occurs after a network call. It arrives as a stream `Err`, not as the error from `invoke` that section 7.5 promises. | Why it matters: Callers see the error in a different place. | Suggested fix: State this case in section 7.3, and add a test for it.

- **The owned `ModelRequest` stays in memory for the whole stream** - Section 7.3 moves the request into the stream so that the fallback can rebuild it. | Why it matters: The full conversation stays in memory until the stream ends. | Suggested fix: Drop the request after the first successful send.

- **The SDK pin floor is higher than necessary** - `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` 1.148.0 already has `OutputConfig.text_format` (local registry). Check the other native types in that version too. The MSRV does not get worse, because `aws-config` 1.13.3 already declares `rust-version = "1.94.1"`. | Why it matters: A lower floor gives downstream users more choice. The workspace value `rust-version = "1.94"` was already too low before this change. | Suggested fix: Pin the lowest version that compiles. Write a separate Linear issue for the 1.94 / 1.94.1 mismatch.

- **Docs: one README sentence will contradict the probes, and one behaviour is missing** - README line 77 says that Bedrock rejects `$ref`/`$defs` and `anyOf` in general. The native probe accepts them. The docs also do not say that user tools stay callable on native models when `JsonSchema` is set. The forced-tool path forces the synthesized tool, so the model cannot call user tools there. | Why it matters: The docs will give wrong guidance. | Suggested fix: Limit the README sentence to tool input schemas. Document the tool-call difference in the README and in the mdBook.

- **ADR-10 is not mentioned** - The provider now sends a second request without a caller instruction. ADR-10 says that the runner never retries automatically. | Why it matters: A reviewer can read the fallback as a breach of ADR-10. | Suggested fix: Add one paragraph that gives four facts. The fallback changes the request shape. It is logged. It occurs at most once. It never repeats a transient error, and `RetryingModel` keeps that job.

- **The schema keyword list has no default policy** - Section 7.5 tells the builder to check the list against a live probe, but it does not name the keywords to probe. It also does not say what happens to a keyword that nobody probed. | Why it matters: A schema with an unprobed keyword can fail at run time, and rule B does not help. | Suggested fix: Name the keywords to probe: `maxItems`, `minLength`, `uniqueItems`, `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `const`, `allOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `prefixItems`, the boolean schema `true` (from `serde_json::Value`), `title`, integer `minimum` (schemars emits it on every unsigned integer), and recursive `$ref`. State if the rewrite keeps only known keywords (an allowlist) or removes only known bad keywords (a denylist).

### QUESTIONS

- What `maxTokens` did each probe in section 2 use?
- On `ConverseStream`, does the forced-choice rejection come back as HTTP 400 from `send()`, or as an event in the stream?
- Does native output accept a recursive `$ref`? If not, is the result an error, as for map types?
- Does `JsonSchemaDefinition.name` have character or length limits? The core takes this name from the schemars `title`.
- Section 2 has no row that shows that Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 accept a forced `toolChoice`, but anti-goal 3 depends on it. Can you add that probe row?
- The direct Anthropic provider also sends a forced `tool_choice` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-839/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/mod.rs:142-144`). Does it have the same defect on these two models? If yes, do you plan a follow-up Linear issue?
- Rule B learns per handle. A short-lived handle, for example one handle per eval case, sends one rejected request each time. Is that acceptable, or do you want a process-wide set keyed by model ID? (The Temporal worker shares one `Arc` per agent, so long-lived workers are not affected.)

## What's good
- `build_request` gets `OutputPath` as an input and does not compute it. That gives a clean and testable seam for both rules.
- The anti-goals are explicit and testable. The snapshot that keeps Sonnet 5 and Haiku 5.5 on the forced tool is the correct guard for anti-goal 3.
- The probes are concrete and include the schema limits. Map types fail with an error and do not change silently. Keep that principle, and apply it to the collapsed shapes in the first BLOCKER.
